claims.quote: The Lakenheath-Bentwaters Incident was a series of radar and visual contacts with unidentified flying objects over airbases in eastern England on the night of 13–14 August 1956, involving personnel from the Royal Air Force (RAF) and the United States Air Force (USAF).

The Lakenheath-Bentwaters Incident was a series of radar and visual contacts with unidentified flying objects over airbases in eastern England on the night of 13–14 August 1956, involving personnel from the Royal Air Force (RAF) and the United States Air Force (USAF).
The incident began at the USAF-tenanted RAF Bentwaters, Suffolk, on the evening of 13 August 1956.
At 21:30, radar operators at the base tracked a target, appearing similar to a normal aircraft return, approaching the base from the sea at an apparent speed of several thousand miles per hour.

claims.v: none in the early period except a single amber star-like object

claims.v: 02:00 and 02:40 on 14 August
claims.quote: The aircrews involved all flew with 23 Squadron from RAF Waterbeach and were scrambled at 02:00 and 02:40 on 14 August – around two hours later than Wimbledon and Perkins claimed the interceptions occurred.

claims.v: scrambles were around two hours later than Wimbledon and Perkins claimed the interceptions occurred
claims.quote: The aircrews involved all flew with 23 Squadron from RAF Waterbeach and were scrambled at 02:00 and 02:40 on 14 August – around two hours later than Wimbledon and Perkins claimed the interceptions occurred.

claims.v: around 10 minutes
claims.quote: The pilot of the first Venom achieved contact, but then found that the target manoeuvred behind him and chased the aircraft for a period of around 10 minutes despite the latter's taking violent evasive action

claims.v: radar contacts were unimpressive and no 'tail-chase' or action on the part of the target occurred
claims.quote: In contrast to the reports given in the original classified teleprinter message and in the accounts of both Wimbledon and Perkins, the aircrews both stated that the radar contacts obtained were unimpressive and that no 'tail-chase', or action on the part of the target, occurred.

claims.v: no visual contacts were made
claims.quote: They also asserted no visual contacts were made.

claims.v: three sets on the ground and one in the intercepting aircraft (per Wimbledon)
claims.quote: Wimbledon disagreed with Klass' analysis, remembering the incident as involving a solid radar return tracked from three sets on the ground and one in the intercepting aircraft.

claims.v: little information emerged until the late 1970s, when newspaper articles produced further witnesses
claims.quote: Little information emerged on the case until the late 1970s, when an article in the Daily Express, and a subsequent piece by astronomer Ian Ridpath in the Sunday Times, produced further witnesses.

claims.v: the incident, or incidents, were much more complex than the Condon Report had suggested
claims.quote: Four British Fortean researchers, Dr. David Clarke, Andy Roberts, Martin Shough, and Jenny Randles, have since conducted a study that has indicated that the incident, or incidents, were much more complex than the Condon Report had suggested.

claims.v: another Venom crew had been scrambled much earlier in the evening
claims.quote: To add to the contradictory nature of the accounts collected, another Venom crew was traced who had been scrambled much earlier in the evening.

claims.v: Davis and another pilot were the two described in Wimbledon's and Perkins' accounts
claims.quote: As the interception would have occurred at the same time as that described by Wimbledon and Perkins, it has been suggested that Davis and another pilot were the two described in their accounts.

claims.v: the most likely conclusion is that radar spoofing technology was being tested
claims.quote: Since the officers and pilots did not make visual contact with the objects, the most likely conclusion is that radar spoofing technology was being tested.

claims.v: probability that at least one genuine UFO was involved appears to be fairly high
claims.quote: "In conclusion, although conventional or natural explanations certainly cannot be ruled out, the probability of such seems low in this case and the probability that at least one genuine UFO was involved appears to be fairly high"
